text:
maria: seeing intermittent packet loss and p95 spikes from gpu-pool-3 in us-west-2 since ~03:10 UTC. apps reporting retransmits and 10-30% request timeouts. traces point at east-west between pod A -> pod B (same AZ). filing here before paging NOC.

maria: quick logs: ping -s 1200 between hosts
```
PING 10.10.34.21 (10.10.34.21): 1200 data bytes
--- 10.10.34.21 ping statistics ---
100 packets transmitted, 95 packets received, 5% packet loss, time 99585ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.123/1.05/15.432/0.98 ms
```

maria: tcpdump on host showed repeated "geneve: checksum error" and fragmented packets before kernel drop:
```
10:12:14.123456 IP host1 > host2: IP 10.10.34.21 > 10.10.34.22: frag 0: proto UDP 1200 data
10:12:14.123457 geneve: bad checksum 0x0000
```

raj: thanks - first instincts: MTU mismatch or offload mismatch (GSO/GRO/LRO). did we push any ToR config/maintenance in west?

olivia: ethtool -k on both NICs? also check ip link show dev geneve0 mtu and host dev mtu.

kevin: we had a rolling ToR OS upgrade starting 03:00 for west-rack-4, could be related. ops-bot posted link to maintenance: https://infra.ops/changes/7891 (started 03:00, small bootstrap script touched interface configs).

maria: running quick checks now:
```
# on host (gpu-node-12)
ip link show dev eth0
eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
ip link show dev geneve0
geneve0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep "gro|gso|lro|rx-checksumming|tx-checksumming"
rx-checksumming: on\ntx-checksumming: on\nscatter-gather: on\ngso: on\ngro: on
```

maria: geneve0 mtu is 1450 but host eth0 is 9000 - expected: overlay reduces inner MTU but 1450 seems too small for our jumbo traffic. However ToR change might have set some physical links to 1500 during upgrade causing fragmentation.

raj: that combination can produce weird drops when offloads are on. if host NIC expects jumbo and ToR strips, large skbs get fragmented with checksums failing. try disabling GRO/GSO on affected host as a quick test.

olivia: run: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off` on one node and see if retransmits stop for pods scheduled there. also tail dmesg for checksum/geneve errors.

maria: disabling gso/gro on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-13 now.

ops-bot: ALERT cleared: network->packet-loss spike for gpu-pool-3 (duration ~12m)

maria: after disabling offloads, ping test: 100/100, 0% loss. application p95 dropped back to normal within 30s. looks like offload + ToR mtu mismatch.

kevin: confirmed with networking team: one ToR got MTU set to 1500 during the OS upgrade where expected value is 9000. they rolled back the ToR config to 9000 at 03:28 UTC.

raj: next steps: 1) re-enable gso/gro on nodes after ToR fix and monitor; 2) add pre-checks to ToR upgrade playbook to assert MTU; 3) file a short postmortem.

maria: re-enabled gso/gro at 03:40, no regression observed for 20m. metrics look stable. will open a postmortem draft and assign to net-eng + infra. thanks all. :thumbsup:

olivia: can we add a K8s node-level check that validates overlay MTU contraints before scheduling large-batch GPU pods? created ticket INFRA-1229.

maria: noted, adding to postmortem and triage. incident resolved, monitoring will keep an eye for 2h. :white_check_mark:
